key_insight: Zatom-2 is a unified atomistic generative foundation model that pretrains on both molecular and material structures to improve generation, prediction, and cross-domain transfer.
engineering_relevance: This matters because a single pretrained model can reduce data needs and improve design workflows across chemistry, materials discovery, and protein engineering.
method: Pretrained on ~5 million structures from OMol25 and OMat24.
Uses a multiscale Transformer with conditional flow matching.
Supports force conditioning plus generation, structure prediction, and energy/force prediction.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved molecular distribution fidelity over Zatom-1, strong benchmark performance for molecule and material generation, and protein backbone designability rising from 67.8% to 74.8% after finetuning on 2,000 protein domains.
watch_item: Performance gains may depend on large-scale pretraining data and task-specific finetuning, so transfer to new domains or sparse-data settings may still require careful validation.
paper_title: Zatom-2: Multitask Pretraining on Atomistic Data for Generative Modeling across Domains
